memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Early the next morning Abraham got up and returned to the place where he had stood before the Lord. He looked down toward Sodom and Gomorrah, toward all the land of the plain, and he saw dense smoke rising from the land, like smoke from a furnace. - Gen 19:27-28 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Abraham rises early and returns to the very spot where, the day before, he had stood pleading with God for Sodom. He looks toward the plain and sees only "dense smoke rising... like smoke from a furnace." The cities are gone. His bold intercession had not, in the end, spared them - because not even ten righteous people were found there.

This is a poignant moment. Abraham had prayed earnestly, appealing to God's mercy again and again. And still, judgement came. What do we make of prayers that seem to go unanswered as we hoped?

We should notice that Abraham's prayers were not wasted. The next verse tells us that God remembered Abraham and rescued Lot precisely because of Abraham's relationship with Him. Abraham asked God to spare the righteous - and God did save the one righteous man there. God answered the heart of Abraham's prayer, even when the cities themselves could not be spared.

There is comfort here for our own prayers. Sometimes God's answer looks different from what we asked, yet He is faithfully working out something good within it. Our intercession is never wasted; it moves the heart of God, even when His response surprises us. Abraham stood again where he had prayed - and we too can keep returning to God, trusting that "the prayer of a righteous person is powerful and effective" (Jas 5:16), even when the outcome is not what we imagined.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Have you had prayers answered differently than you hoped?
- Can you trust that God is faithfully at work even in surprising answers?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, when my prayers are answered differently than I hoped, help me trust that You are faithfully at work. Thank You that my intercession is never wasted. Keep me returning to stand before You in prayer.
Amen.
